blocks.text: Keysville Town Council
Regular Meeting of September 14, 2026
REGULAR MEETING OF THE KEYSVILLE TOWN COUNCIL
HELD ON SEPTEMBER 14, 2026

The Keysville Town Council held its regular meeting on Monday, September 14, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at the Keysville Town Office. Mayor Robert J. Schaefer presided, with Vice Mayor Anthony Ferranto and Council Members Wendy Gallion, Rhonda Benn, Rachael Clark, and Tom Fisher were present. Council Member Scotty Jackson called in remotely. Staff present included Stephanie Clay, Town Manager, and Sherry Marker, Town Clerk; Eric Traywick and Liz Peaden were in attendance.
Mayor Schaefer called the meeting to order and welcomed all in attendance. Council Member Benn offered the invocation.
Public Comments
Christmas Door Decorating

Mrs. Peaden represented the Garden Club and asked if the Town would be giving the Christmasdoor-decorating cash prizes, as has been done in previous years. The Town Council stated that the cash prizes would be given this year.
Traffic Signage

Mrs. Peaden also spoke as a Town resident regarding traffic signage. She stated that on I Street and the alley, she had observed a vehicle fail to stop because there was no stop sign in place. She also noted that the stop sign at the end of I Street at King Street, near Dan Farnsworth residence, was missing. Mayor Schaefer stated that the Town would check into the matter.
Yard Debris Collection
Mr. Traywick asked if someone would be available to collect weeds, bushes, and yard cuttings once residents cleaned up their yards.

Mayor Schaefer stated that a sign-up sheet had been provided the previous year for yard debris collection, but no one had signed up. Mayor Schaefer said he would check with the County to see if a dumpster could be provided and whether a designated location could be established for residents to dispose of the yard debris.
Minutes
Motion to approve July and August 2026 minutes was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Fisher. The motion was carried unanimously.
Motion to approve July 13, 2026, Public Hearing minutes was made by Council Member Gallion and seconded by Council Member Benn. The motion was carried unanimously.
Financials
Motion was made by Council Member Gallion and seconded by Vice Mayor Ferranto to approve the July 2026 financials and pay the bills. The motion was carried unanimously.
Motion was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Gallion to approve the August 2026 financials and pay the bills. The motion was carried unanimously.
Committee Reports
• Streets and Library Committee — Hill Avenue Sidewalk
Council Member Benn asked about the update on the sidewalk on Hill Avenue. Mrs. Clay said the window for the application had passed and the next round of funds would be in 2028.
• Park Update — Playground Equipment Repairs
• Mrs. Clay informed Council that two pieces of playground equipment, the dragon slide and

the twisted tube, need repairs. She stated that the equipment with the spring could be repaired. Mrs. Clay contacted GameTime and received a quote of $5,200.00 for the necessary parts. She is still waiting on a separate quote for installation.
• Water Committee
Nothing to report
• Wastewater Committee
Nothing to report
Old Business
Tower Park Pear Tree Removal
Motion was made by Council Member Gallion and seconded by Vice Mayor Ferranto to remove the pear tree at Tower Park with Southern Hills Lawn Care for $750.00. Motion was carried unanimously.
Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) The Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) would resume its cycle in December 2026.
Website Provider
Motion was made by Vice Mayor Ferranto and seconded by Council Member Gallion to switch to a new website provider, which is Revize. The cost would be $1500.00. Motion was carried unanimously.
New Business
National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)

Mrs. Clay asked the Council if they would like the Town to participate in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). She explained that participation would benefit the citizens and would not cost the Town anything.
A motion was made by Vice Mayor Ferranto and seconded by Council Member Fisher to adopt a resolution to participate in the NFIP. The motion carried unanimously.
Halloween

Halloween will be observed in the Town on October 31st from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. The hours will be published in the Charlotte Gazette, on the Town’s website, and on Facebook. The Sheriff's Department will also be notified of the designated hours.
Christmas Parade
The monetary amounts used for the Christmas Parade last year will remain the same for this year.
Lawnmower
The purchase of a new lawnmower was tabled until next month’s meeting pending additional information.
Hometown Hero Banner

Mrs. Clay said Landon Greene had contacted her to see if the Town would be interested in participating in the Hometown Hero Banner program. She asked the Council if they would like her to pursue additional information.
A motion was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Gallion to pursue additional information regarding the Hometown Hero Banners. The motion carried unanimously.

9176 Church Street Property Mrs. Clay said she had spoken with Milton Jones, the owner of the derelict property located at 9176 Church Street. Mr. Jones stated that he may be willing to sign the property over to the Town.
A motion was made by Vice Mayor Ferranto and seconded by Council Member Gallion to pursue having the property signed over to the Town. The motion carried unanimously.
Back Office Parking Lot

Mrs. Clay asked the Council if they would approve the cleanup of the back-office parking lot. Southern Hills had provided a quote of $500; however, Mrs. Clay stated that she would have the company provide an updated quote.
A motion was made by Council Member Benn and seconded by Council Member Fisher to approve the cleanup of the back-office parking lot up to $1500.00. The motion carried unanimously.
Mayor’s Report
Town Manager Report Given throughout the meeting.
Next Meeting
Because the regularly scheduled Town Council meeting falls on the holiday of October 12, 2026, the meeting was postponed to Monday, October 19, 2026.
Adjournment
Council Member Benn made a motion, and Council Member Fisher seconded, to adjourn the meeting. The meeting was adjourned at 8:30 p.m.
